instructions: The night before: move the phyllo from the freezer to the fridge so it thaws slowly. Leave it in its box.

In the morning, heat the oven to 325°F with a rack in the middle. Melt the 1/2 cup butter in a small pan over low heat, then take it off the heat. Brush the bottom and sides of an 8 inch square baking dish with a little of it.
In a medium bowl, whisk the 2 eggs, 1/2 cup sugar, 1/2 cup flour and the pinch of salt into a smooth, thick paste with no dry flour left.
Pour the 2 cups milk into a medium saucepan and add the 1/2 tsp vanilla. Heat it over medium heat until it steams and small bubbles appear around the edge, about 5 minutes. Don't let it boil.
Pour about a third of the hot milk into the egg bowl in a thin stream, whisking the whole time. Keep whisking, or the eggs will scramble.

Pour the egg mixture back into the saucepan and turn the heat to medium low. Whisk without stopping for 2 to 3 minutes, until it's as thick as pudding and a few slow bubbles break the surface. Take it off the heat and give it a stir every few minutes while you do the pastry, so no skin forms.
Unroll the phyllo and keep it covered with a clean, damp kitchen towel as you work. It dries out fast when it's left open.
Lay one sheet in the dish so the ends hang over two sides, and drizzle it with a spoonful of the butter. Repeat with 4 more sheets, buttering each one.
Pour in the custard and smooth the top. Fold the overhanging ends of phyllo in over the custard.
Lay 5 more sheets on top, buttering each one, and tuck the edges down the sides of the dish. Brush the top with the rest of the butter.
With a sharp knife, score the top into 8 squares, cutting through the top layers of pastry only.
Bake for 40 to 45 minutes, until it's puffed, crisp and deep golden all over.
Let it cool in the dish for 15 minutes so the custard sets enough to cut.
Dust it with the 2 tbsp powdered sugar through a small sieve, then sprinkle over the 1/2 tsp cinnamon. Cut along the scored lines and serve warm.
advance_prep_notes: Thaw the phyllo in the fridge overnight, the night before.
method_notes: Both versions make a vanilla custard on the stove, wrap it in buttered phyllo, bake it until crisp and golden, and finish it with powdered sugar and cinnamon while warm. My Greek Dish (the lead) thickens milk with eggs, sugar and flour and bakes it as a layered tray pie at 320°F for 45 minutes; Super Golden Bakes uses condensed milk, cream and semolina and rolls the custard into individual parcels. This is the lead at half size in an 8 inch dish for four, with the pinch of salt Super Golden Bakes adds; it takes about an hour and a half with the cooling, so it suits a weekend morning. The lead's 664 is a reviewCount, not a ratingCount.
